name: navigation-menu
description: A horizontal site navigation bar with dropdown panels. Built on Radix UI NavigationMenu. Three component sets: nav-button (trigger or link), nav-panel (dropdown panel), and nav-panel-link (link row inside panel).

nav-button.purpose: Clickable item in the nav bar — Type=Trigger (opens panel) or Type=Link (navigates directly).

nav-panel-link.purpose: Individual link row inside nav-panel — State=Default/Focus/Hover/Disabled.

intent.Trigger: Opens a nav-panel dropdown. Has leading icon + label + trailing chevron.
intent.Link: Navigates directly. Has leading icon + label. No chevron, no dropdown.

intent.List: Single column of up to 3 nav-panel-link instances + 2 extra SLOTs.
intent.Grid: Two columns (column-left, column-right), each with 3 links + 1 SLOT.
intent.Featured: featured SLOT (160px, image/callout) alongside column of 3 links + 1 SLOT.

navButton.note: Use color/background/* tokens on nav-button — it sits on the page canvas, not a surface.

composition.navButtonTrigger: H AUTO-LAYOUT: icon (16×16) → label → chevron (16×16). Chevron present in Trigger type only.
composition.navButtonLink: H AUTO-LAYOUT: icon (16×16) → label. No chevron.
composition.navPanelList: V AUTO-LAYOUT: link-1 → link-2 → link-3 → extra-4 SLOT → extra-5 SLOT
composition.navPanelGrid: H AUTO-LAYOUT: column-left (3 links + extra-2 SLOT) + column-right (3 links + extra-3 SLOT)
composition.navPanelFeatured: H AUTO-LAYOUT: featured SLOT (160px) + links-column (3 links + extra-1 SLOT)

behavior.openDelay: 200ms hover delay before panel opens (Radix UI NavigationMenu default: delayDuration=200)
behavior.closeGrace: 300ms grace period when cursor moves from trigger toward panel (skipDelayDuration=300)
behavior.escapeDismiss: Escape closes panel and returns focus to the trigger
behavior.oneAtATime: Only one NavigationMenuContent open at a time — opening a second closes the first
behavior.animation: data-motion='from-start'/'from-end' on panel for directional enter/exit animation
behavior.viewport: NavigationMenuViewport renders panel inside a shared viewport positioned below the trigger list, repositioning to align with the active trigger

accessibility.trigger: NavigationMenuTrigger renders <button aria-expanded aria-controls> — expanded state announced automatically
accessibility.panel: NavigationMenuContent has aria-labelledby pointing to its trigger
accessibility.links: NavigationMenuLink renders <a> — use asChild with router Link for SPA navigation
accessibility.focusTrap: Panel is NOT a modal — focus is not trapped; Tab moves through all panel links
keyboard: Tab to move between nav items
Enter/Space to activate trigger or follow link
Escape to close panel and return focus to trigger
Arrow Right/Left to move between trigger list items
Arrow Down to move into open panel content
Home/End to first/last item in trigger list

constraints: Use Type=Trigger only when there is a nav-panel to open — never a trigger with no associated content.
Use Type=Link for direct-navigation items (About, Pricing, Contact).
Layout=List for ≤5 links; Layout=Grid for 6–12 links; Layout=Featured for a strong visual anchor.
Always provide both title and description in nav-panel-link.
Keep nav bar to 5–7 triggers/links maximum.
Place <NavigationMenu> once per page — in site header layout, not inside a page component.
Never nest a NavigationMenuTrigger inside NavigationMenuContent — navigation menus are one level deep.
Use NavigationMenuLink with asChild + router Link in Next.js/React Router for proper SPA navigation.

useCases: A SaaS app header has 'Products', 'Solutions', and 'Pricing' — Products and Solutions each expand to a panel of sub-links
A marketing site top nav includes 'Features' (opens a grid of feature links), 'Docs' (direct link), and 'Blog' (direct link)
A platform nav bar shows 'Integrations' with a featured panel highlighting a new integration alongside a list of categories
An enterprise app header organises a large link library into two columns under each top-level trigger
A documentation site uses a nav bar with trigger buttons that reveal categorised article links in a list panel
A commerce site's top nav shows 'Collections' with a featured image panel linking to seasonal categories

Trigger.whenToUse: Top-level nav item that opens a dropdown panel of sub-links
examples: 'Products' with a panel of product categories

Link.whenToUse: Top-level route that navigates directly without a dropdown

Featured.whenToUse: One nav section has a strong visual anchor alongside sub-links

comparedTo.situation: Horizontal top nav bar with dropdown panels for site-level navigation
Persistent vertical nav along the left edge of a product layout
Within-page section switching that stays on the same URL
Shows the user's current location in a page hierarchy

notes: nav-button uses color/background/* tokens (not color/surface/*) because it sits on the page canvas, not a component surface.

changelog.change: Panel link title token corrected: color/surface/default/foreground → color/surface/overlay/foreground (paired-surface fix — panel fills with color/surface/overlay).

darkMode.notes: Panel link title uses color/surface/overlay/foreground (corrected from surface/default/foreground). Both resolve identically in light mode (#18181b) but differ in dark.
darkMode.pairedSurfaceRisk: color/surface/overlay/foreground — must pair with color/surface/overlay (panel background). Using surface/default/foreground would break in dark mode.

notes: Viewport uses max-w-max on root + flex justify-center — panel centers under nav bar, not individual trigger.
